podcast.title: Forgotten by 1952
podcast.body: Despite being very popular in the 1920s, The Carter Family was largely forgotten by 1952, when Harry Smith compiled his "Anthology of American Folk Music." "by 1952 even the most popular act, like Blind Lemon Jefferson or The Carter Family, were largely forgotten."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 97: "Song to Woody" by Bob Dylan

podcast.title: Big Name Act on Old Dominion Barn Dance
podcast.body: The Carter Family was among the "big name acts" that performed on the Old Dominion Barn Dance, a tier below the Louisiana Hayride and Grand Ole Opry in the country music hierarchy. "The Barn Dance had some big name acts, the Carter family."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 40: "Drugstore Rock 'n' Roll" by Janis Martin

podcast.title: Influence on Robert Johnson's Musical Philosophy
podcast.body: Bob Dylan acknowledged that many of Woody Guthrie's songs he loved were rewrites of old Carter Family songs, providing a justification for Robert Johnson's reinterpretation of other blues artists' material. "many of the woody got these songs he loved, were rewrites of old Carter family songs, so if Johnson was rewriting Lee Roy Car songs that was fair enough."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 97: "Song to Woody" by Bob Dylan

podcast.title: Influence on Woody Guthrie
podcast.body: Woody Guthrie's early career as a country singer was inspired by The Carter Family, among other 1920s greats. "Guthrie had started out as a country singer, singing songs inspired by the Carter family, Jimmy Rogers, and other 1920s greats."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
